cands.name: Heath Allbright

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.

cands.bio: Republican state representative for Alabama House District 11 since August 2025, after winning a special election. Owns Brighton Forestry Services, a timber harvesting and reforestation company in Holly Pond. Previously served on the Cullman County Board of Education.

endorsements.text: Wikipedia reports his 2025 special-election campaign was supported by the Business Council of Alabama, the Alabama Forestry Association and the Alabama Farmers Federation.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or when, if ever, he moved to Alabama. We found no documented actions or stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored came through empty, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2025 or 2026. The only position statements found were a Wikipedia summary of a forum (cutting the state income tax, local book restrictions on sexually explicit books, opposition to transgender athletes). Those do not match the issues we track and rest on a secondary source, so we left them out. We found no photo, no documented controversies, and no foreign ties.

qual.background: Alabama House member since August 2025; two terms on the Cullman County Board of Education (first won in 2016); owner of a timber harvesting and reforestation business; worked in forestry; associate degree from Northwest Shoals Community College (2005).
qual.why: He has about a year of legislative service, plus local elected office and business ownership. He has no law, policy or budget career on the record and no chamber leadership role, so the score is below the top range.
